a_t1.text: GlassineOS hub — revised against the prototype

a_n1.text:
Exists in hub: five layers from config/repos.toml + Unplaced; per-repo issues, PRs, CI state, last commit, release; org totals; docs index state.

Proposed (feasible):
• Run strip = last 10 runs per repo (REST, one call/repo)
• Repo detail pane with issues by label
• API budget in the header (GET /rate_limit, free)
• 'Needs you' queue — the waiting-agent row needs the Notification hook (see Shells)

a_n2.text:
Exists: org project as a board, move between status columns.

Fix (known gap 1): 'Add to board' + new strategic issue lands on the board — return the item node ID from create.

Proposed: a rollup per repo on each card, counting the issues whose body says “Part of GlassineOS/hub#N” (one issue search per card). No GitHub sub-issue links.

a_n3.text:
List and item no longer share the screen.
• Work is a full-width list, grouped by what needs you, with a one-click Claude action on every row.
• Opening an item gives it the whole page (second row: Work item): header, actions, Claude actions, then Conversation · Checks · Files with a narrow details column. k / j steps to the next item without going back.
• The Steward sidebar is open on the list and folds to its rail on the item; it still follows the selection.

Exists in hub: everything in the action bars except the Claude buttons. Close gaps: assignee filter, label editing, Markdown rendering.

a_n4.text:
Exists: semantic search, index state (current / building / stale / failed), start docs CI, auto-dispatch once per commit after 15 min stale.

Proposed: show which commit each state refers to and the auto-dispatch countdown — both already known to the app.

a_n5.text:
Exists: tmux sessions (-L glassine-hub) on hubd's host with a start command; agent shells get the tool-server URL + token.

Proposed:
• Managed sessions carry a manifest (persona, model, prompt, skills, tool scopes) that hub stores and shows
• Per-session token scoped to the tool groups the persona allows — enforced in hubd, so a session can't widen its own rights by editing settings
• 'Waiting' via a Claude Code Notification hook to the loopback tool server; the UI only jumps you to the prompt
• Plain shells stay first-class

a_n6.text:
Advanced mode. Opens pre-filled with the planner's spec; every field maps to stock Claude Code: --model, --permission-mode, --mcp-config (hub tools + scoped token), --settings, --append-system-prompt (persona), first prompt as argument, skills linked into .claude/skills.

'Save as preset' turns a hand-tuned spec into a new one-click action.

Fable for audits: its cyber safeguards may limit exploit-level detail; defensive review of your own code is the intended use.

a_n8.text:
One-click sessions. Each item offers context actions (PR: review, fix checks, prepare for merge; issue: triage, implement, draft docs; run: investigate, flakiness).

A click runs a throwaway planner: claude -p, read-only tools, structured JSON output. It reads the item and returns the spec: persona, model, mode, worktree, skills, tool scopes, first prompt.

The planner reads untrusted text (PR bodies, logs), so hubd validates the spec against a schema and clamps it to a fixed ceiling per action — a review can never gain merge or push. Personas come from a list, never free text.

Option per action: start without confirming.

The planner run has its own model — Opus, Sonnet or Haiku — picked in Notes & context (Work item) or next to the agent model (new-work modal). Separate from the agent's model on the spec.

a_n9.text:
Embedded sessions. A session opens in the view that spawned it (here under the item). 'Send to background' only detaches that view: the tmux session keeps running, the row shows a session marker, and Sessions lists it with where it came from. 'Bring back' re-attaches.

Feasible as-is: tmux allows several clients on one session, so the same session can be embedded in Work and open in Sessions at once. Hub stores origin (view + item) with the session.

a_n10.text:
The Steward is a configured session, nothing more.
• persona Steward · Sonnet by default (change it from the model name in the sidebar header) · resumed with --continue · memory in the hub repo (orchestrator/journal.md, plans/<week>.md, decisions/).
• Its hub write tools are set to ask, so every write shows up as an ordinary permission card (hub.create_issue …).
• It plans work with the same planner tools every agent has (a draft you open in the new-work modal) and starts sessions through the same planner and ceilings as a click.
• It learns what changed by reading hub when you ask or when it works — there is no event stream.
• Its questions don't time out.

a_n11.text:
One sidebar, on every screen — the Steward's session, no tabs.
• WAITING FOR YOU: its open questions and permission prompts (the shared interaction card) and the new work it drafted (open in the planner, or Not now).
• Then the terminal, preset messages and an input. Collapsed, it's a rail: S with the waiting count, and ＋.
• It follows you: SEES chips are the screen and selection, passed with each question by the UserPromptSubmit hook. Configure opens its session spec like any other.

a_n12.text:
Send buttons. Each button is a message you send: hub pastes it into the session with tmux paste-buffer (bracketed, so multi-line arrives as one prompt).
• Only when idle — the Stop / Notification hooks tell hub; clicks during a turn are queued, never typed over output.
• Interrupt = Esc, the one key Claude Code handles cleanly. Never Ctrl-C.
• Only people press them. The Steward never sends into a child session; it reads summaries.
• Presets per persona live next to the persona files and are editable.

Answers to prompts reach the session through the hook that asked — nothing is typed for them.

a_n13.text:
Comments with Claude.
• Draft with Claude / Summarise thread / Reply with Claude are throwaway claude -p runs with read-only tools. They fill a draft; nothing is posted until you press Comment or Post reply.
• Address review: tick threads (or take all open ones) → the planner writes an implementation spec for the PR's own branch with those threads in the prompt. The agent pushes fixups and drafts one reply per thread for you; it never resolves threads itself.
• Reviews by agent sessions post as you, and GitHub won't let a PR's author review it formally — so they arrive as review comments, which is exactly what this flow consumes.

a_n14.text:
How it's wired (verified in the prototype)
• A PermissionRequest hook forwards the prompt to hub and waits; the terminal prompt stays up. First answer wins: hub card or terminal.
• Allow → tool runs. Deny → tool doesn't run, Claude gets your reason. Timeout (10 min) → nothing approved, terminal-only.
• AskUserQuestion goes the same way; Claude sees the chosen option or your own text.

Proposed on top: 'Always allow' writes a session rule; the Steward's questions have no timeout and also pin in its sidebar.

a_n15.text:
The badge
• Sessions in the top nav counts every unanswered prompt across all sessions, the Steward included, plus new work an agent drafted. It links to Needs you.
• The Steward's rail shows its own count.
• Answering anywhere (inbox, embedded session, sidebar, terminal) clears it everywhere: hubd holds one record per prompt.

a_n16.text:
New work is a modal, opened over whatever you're looking at and prefilled from it (Work list, Work item, Roadmap, Overview repo detail, Steward sidebar ＋). Agents open it too: any session can draft new work for you.

It runs in four stages, shown as a rail on the left:
1 Configure — template, repo/scope, notes, pins, planner model, who gets the drafts.
2 Review the plan — the planner (claude -p, ~1 min) writes a spec; you check persona, checkout, tools, ceiling, docs context and the first prompt, pick the agent model, re-plan or go back. Nothing has run yet.
3 Session — the real Claude session, embedded, 20–40 min for an audit. Its questions show up in the modal; Send to background at any time.
4 Drafts — pick and file, or hand to the Steward. A backgrounded run's drafts wait in Sessions › Needs you ('Drafts ready') and reopen the modal at this stage.

a_n18.text:
History & cleanup.
• Resume: Claude Code keeps transcripts per folder (~/.claude/projects/…); hub stores session id + worktree path. Resume = new tmux window running claude --resume <id> in that folder. If the worktree was removed, hubd re-adds it at the same path from its branch first.
• Cleanup is a new hubd capability, limited to ~/hub-worktrees, shown as exact commands before it runs. git refuses dirty worktrees and unmerged branches, so 'Review first' rows fail safely.
• Transcripts are never deleted here — that keeps everything resumable.

a_t5.text: New work: configure → review the plan → session → drafts

a_n19.text: Suggestions instead of refusals. When you ask the Steward to start work, it calls suggest_session(action, issues, notes, why) — the same pattern as drafting new work. A card lands in its sidebar and in Sessions › Needs you: 'Implement epd#9, also covering epd#11', with its reason and proposed notes. Open the start form opens the normal form, filled in; nothing runs until you press Start.

a_n20.text:
Sessions ↔ issues is many-to-many (UI only; hub stores a list per session).
• A session has a primary issue and 'also covers' issues. The start form, the Work item planner (Also covers) and the Steward's suggestion all set it.
• Every covered issue shows the session in Work ('impl-epd-9-11 · also covers'); one issue can show several sessions ('2 sessions · kernel-lut, review-kernel-212').
• The session is told to close all of them, and its PR body lists 'Closes #9 · Closes #11'.

arch.text: Archive — earlier iterations, kept unchanged. Do not implement from these; see Read me › “Where the earlier boards went”.

s4.text:
Every screen = Header + its content + Steward sidebar. All numbers, refs and sessions come from data/fixtures.js, so the Needs you count (9), the Steward’s count (4), Work rows and Needs you always agree.

Every Launch button on these screens opens the same Launch component; only its prefill differs.

c1.text: Components — change one, every screen changes

c2.text: Each component’s props are its tweaks (Launch: entry, stage, action, covers, by; Interaction: iid, status; SessionView: sid, size). Import order: Interaction ← SessionView ← Launch ← Feed / Header / Steward.

f1.text: Flows — the same components, pinned to a stage

c3.text: Scale rule: no screen lists every repository as pills or buttons. Repo choices go through RepoPicker (type to filter, recent and failing first, layer chips, single or multi). Items go through ItemPicker: by meaning on the work-item index, or GitHub search as soon as you type a qualifier (repo:, is:, label:) or a ref.

s5.text: Notes — what the project has learned, and how far to trust it

s6.text: Phone — the same screens at 390 px

s7.text:
Notes is the read-only view of notes find. Agents — the Steward included — read and add to the same notes with the notes command, so the Steward stays on this page.

Keep notes useful (right column) starts compaction and the docs sweep by hand, for all notes or one topic.

It stays a separate tab from Knowledge on purpose: words only, run with a button; the index updates itself in the background, shown by a small badge, 20 rows then up to 100, and the search is not kept in the address.

Diary rows past the first dozen are filler to show the 40- and 340-row states.

c4.text:
Persona families: build (blue), review (violet), investigate (orange), write (green), organise (grey). The icon tells personas apart within a family; the name is always in text.

Sessions that share an item link to each other: header row “Also on these items”, ⇄ in the Sessions list, persona tabs on the item page.

c5.text:
Two kinds of button, never mixed:
• Blue = start an agent (Launch).
• Black split button with the commit symbol = something you do yourself on GitHub. The most relevant action is inline; the arrow lists the rest. Disabled items say why (e.g. Merge: checks running · not approved). Merge and Close confirm.
